card.name: Sattriya
card.era: Created 15th-16th century by Srimanta Sankardev; classical status 2000
card.profile: Sattriya (Sattriya Nritya) is a major Indian classical dance created in the 15th-16th century by the Assamese saint-scholar Srimanta Sankardev as part of Bhaona - performances of Ankiya Nat one-act plays (Wikipedia). It developed and was preserved within Sattras, the Vaishnavite monasteries of Assam, where monks performed dance-dramas on the legends of Krishna and other avatars of Vishnu drawn from texts such as the Bhagavata Purana (Wikipedia). Integrating nritta, nritya and natya, it traces its theoretical roots to the Natya Shastra and was historically performed by male monks before moving to the public stage.
card.insight: The Sangeet Natak Akademi formally recognized Sattriya as one of India's classical dances on 15 November 2000, and the tradition remains a living practice of the Ekasarana Dharma communities of Assam's sattras (Wikipedia).
